title: Router Boot Process: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A router starts up much like a smartphone. It goes through a set order of steps. The order is easy to learn.

scenes.heading: Boot order
scenes.narration: Here's what happens. The hardware test runs, called P O S T. The bootloader starts, called R O M mon. It finds the I O S image. It loads the I O S. Then it reads the startup config.

scenes.heading: The config register
scenes.narration: A single register steers it. The default is zero x two one oh two. Zero x two one four two ignores the saved config, for password recovery. And zero x two one zero zero stays in ROM mon.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. P O S T only tests the hardware. The register is stored separately. The boot variable and the register are different.

items.wrong: Register is in the running config

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. P O S T, then R O M mon, then I O S, then config. Zero x two one zero two is the default. Zero x two one four two skips the config. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva booting lab.
